note: The one klt build layout/reports/ is evidence for. Recorded here so a run
can check it *before* producing evidence, instead of naming it after the
fact in layout/reports/environment.json. layout/run_checks.sh refuses to
run against any other build; layout/lvs_reference.py --check-deck-hash
requires every committed report to name this deck. Regenerate after

deck.name: gf180mcu
resolved_by: `klt deck resolve` postdates the pinned release, so klt 0.2.0 itself
cannot run that command; the resolution above was taken from a later
klayout-tools build whose release-history table covers v0.1.0..v0.2.0.
run_checks.sh runs it opportunistically and reports rather than fails
when the subcommand is absent -- the check with teeth is that the klt
on PATH actually produces the content_hash above.

why_the_version_string_is_not_enough: `klt --version` reports the package version, which a source build made
after a tag still carries -- so a post-tag build of klayout-tools and the
released v0.2.0 both say `klt 0.2.0` while shipping different decks. The
deck content hash is what tells them apart. This repo's committed evidence
once named a deck hash no release ships (#258) precisely because only the
version string was ever checked, and then only after the fact.
